Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan for the POC prompt/log handoff.

Goals we heard on the call:
- Evaluate relevance and answer quality for customer-support summarization flows (50–300 token prompts).
- Verify throughput/latency profile for synchronous inference under realistic concurrency (target 95th <= 250ms for single-turn queries).
- Validate that Redwood’s reranking and context-windowing produce >=90% entity extraction F1 on your annotated test set.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Relevance: human-rated relevance >= 4/5 on a 400-sample test set provided by StitchAI.
2) Extraction: entity extraction F1 >= 0.90 on annotated examples.
3) Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for representative 1–3 sentence prompts at the target concurrency.
4) No PII leakage on sampled outputs (we will run a redaction verification step).

Data we need from StitchAI to run the eval and ingest prompts/logs:
- 1,000 sample prompts/logs (anonymized) as a CSV or JSONL with columns/fields: id, session_id (optional), prompt_text, context_snippet (optional), expected_label or expected_answer (if available), timestamp, source_channel.
- A smaller annotated evaluation set (100–400 rows) with ground-truth labels for the relevance and extraction checks.
- Any internal pass/fail rubric you use for relevance or extraction (spreadsheet or doc).

Format and delivery options:
- Preferred: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with UTF-8 and consistent field names. CSV is OK if you include a header.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URL, Google Drive link, or secure ShareFile transfer. We can accept PGP-encrypted attachments if required.

Security / compliance asks:
- Confirm the dataset is anonymized and does not contain raw customer PII. If you need a redaction checklist, we can provide one.
- If you require a DPA or specific security paperwork, loop in procurement (cc’d if applicable).

Proposed timeline and owners:
- Nov 8: StitchAI provides initial sample (min 200 rows).
- Nov 12: Redwood validates schema, confirms ingestion plan and any missing fields (Rishi to run validation).
- Nov 18–27: Ingestion, early eval runs, and initial results share.

Tom / Laura — thanks for the sample. A few technical notes from the ingestion/ops side to make the run smooth: 

1) Preferred ingest format: JSONL (one object per line) with fields: id, session_id, prompt_text, context, expected_answer, timestamp, channel. If you only have CSV, include header names exactly.
2) Context: if prompts are part of a thread, include a context_snippet field with up to 512 tokens. That helps KV caching and semantic chunking.
3) Encoding: UTF-8; normalize whitespace; avoid proprietary control characters.
4) PII: If you can run a quick redaction pass and replace emails/phone numbers with <REDACTED>, that reduces compliance scope. If you need our redaction checklist, we’ll send it.
5) Delivery: S3 presigned URL is easiest for us. If you prefer Drive, please ensure the folder permission is set to the upload link and share with redwood-data@redwoodinference.com.
